UK Budget Announces £100 Energy Support Payment for Households

Eligibility and Scope

Chancellor John Healey has announced a new £100 payment intended to assist households with rising energy costs this winter. The policy primarily targets residents in England living in properties within council tax bands A to D.

Key details regarding eligibility include:

  • Council Tax Bands: Only properties in bands A through D are included in the primary rollout.
  • Students: Those living in student halls are excluded as they are not subject to standard council tax banding. However, students renting private accommodation that falls within the A-D bracket remain eligible.
  • Exemptions: Residents who do not pay council tax due to specific exemptions or those who use payment methods other than direct debit will receive guidance from local authorities on how to receive their payment.

Regional Differences

While the mandate applies specifically to England, the UK government has allocated funding for devolved administrations to implement similar schemes. The current status across the UK is as follows:

  • Wales: The Welsh government has confirmed it will mirror the £100 payment for eligible households.
  • Scotland: The Scottish government has indicated an intention to replicate the policy.
  • Northern Ireland: Implementation remains uncertain as the devolved government currently lacks the legal authority to approve the necessary budget.

Payment Logistics

For households that pay their council tax via direct debit, the funds are scheduled to be deposited directly into the associated bank accounts beginning in early January.

Contextual Financial Outlook

While the government characterizes the payment as cost-of-living support, analysts note the broader economic context. Consultants from Cornwall Insight have projected that average yearly energy bills could increase by between £276 and £400 starting in January.

Verification

Residents are encouraged to verify their specific council tax band status to confirm eligibility. In England, this can be done via the official government postcode search tool. As the government has stated the funds will be issued directly to bank accounts, recipients should remain cautious of potential phishing attempts or requests for personal banking details via unsolicited contact.

Funding for this initiative is sourced from an increase in the bank surcharge on corporation tax, which is set to rise from 3% to 6% for a 15-month period beginning in 2027.
